 204→## Human decision
 205→
 206→A case the Judge withholds — a gate stopped the ruling, or the model could not answer — waits
 207→for a person; `app/human_review.py` owns that decision. The reviewer's action is validated in
 208→code and stored as `human_decision.json` in the run directory, written atomically (a temp file
 209→linked into place) so exactly one of several concurrent requests can decide and a second is
 210→refused. The ceiling is SGD 500: the model's proposed amount has no upper bound, so an approval
 211→above it is refused and the reviewer must use a change instead. No money gate is consulted
 212→again — the gate that held the case does not hold the person — and `case_file.json` and
 213→`dispute.json` are never rewritten. One `human.decision_recorded` event is appended to the
 214→run's log; if that append fails the decision still stands. The party message is built in code:
 215→an approval keeps the proposal's Basis line (the plain titles of the cited rules, escalation
 216→rules excluded), while a change or a rejection never carries one, because the citations may
 217→contradict the person's decision. The reviewer's name and reason never reach a party.
 218→
 219→The operator console presents a review queue for withheld cases, where a reviewer opens a case file and completes a decision form. A local confirm screen restates the chosen action, amount, fare and AI proposal before the reviewer sends it. The Overrides view groups changed and rejected decisions while counting approvals accepted as proposed. The console loads a case through `/api/review/<run_id>/case` and expands server event payloads through `/api/review/<run_id>/payloads/<name>`; both are read-only JSON paths with no-store responses.
 220→
 221→The server exposes the loop as JSON, all `Cache-Control: no-store`:
 222→
 223→| Endpoint | Purpose |
 224→|---|---|
 225→| `POST /api/review/<run_id>/decision` | Store one human decision on a withheld run (works for command-line runs too) |
 226→| `GET /api/review/queue` | Every withheld run with no valid decision, safety cases first, then largest amount, longest wait |
 227→| `GET /api/review/overrides` | Approvals counted; changes and rejections grouped by the shape of the departure |
 228→| `GET /api/disputes/<dispute_id>` | The party's own view of their dispute's current run, with its decision applied |
 229→| `GET /api/demo/rider` | The demo rider account: every dispute filed on this demo |
 230→| `GET /api/demo/driver` | The demo driver account: read-only outcomes for the demo driver's trips |
 231→
 232→Only direct children of the output folder that hold a case file are runs — eval runs live a
 233→level deeper and are never seen — and a dispute's current run is the party-filed run without
 234→`answered.json`, latest `generated_at` first. The pages are clients: `ui/party/status.html`
 235→looks a reference up and answers a round-two question in place, `ui/party/driver.html` is
 236→read-only, and every rule above stays in Python.

 238→## Policy and dataset packs
 239→
 240→`docs/policy.md` is data, not code: rules with IDs (GEN, EV, RD, NS, ESC families),
 241→preconditions written against pack fields in plain language, and per-rule provenance
 242→stating whether a rule comes from Ryde's own published policy, a comparable operator, or
 243→the project team. The pipeline reads it at the path in `app/config.json`; a different
 244→policy document drops in with no code change. Nothing in the code evaluates the
 245→preconditions — the Judge reads the rules and applies them in its reasoning. Citing a rule
 246→that does not exist is recorded rather than blocked: an unknown ID is logged under the
 247→ruling's `validation.unknown_rule_ids` with a note and the ruling still issues, but only
